'''Rusmir Mahmutćehajić''' (29 June 1948 – 5 April 2026) was a Bosnian author, intellectual and politician.<ref name="rusmirmahmutcehajic1">{{cite web |url=http://www.rusmirmahmutcehajic.ba/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=56 |title=Biography |publisher=Rusmirmahmutcehajic.ba |date=29 June 1948 |accessdate=2019-10-17 |archive-date=23 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923010159/http://www.rusmirmahmutcehajic.ba/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=56 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Mahmutćehajić was born in [[Stolac]], [[PR Bosnia and Herzegovina]] on 29 June 1948.<ref name="rusmirmahmutcehajic1" /> He studied [[electrical engineering]] at the [[University of Sarajevo]] and graduated in 1973. He continued his studies at the [[University of Zagreb]] with a focus on the propagation of [[Electromagnetic radiation|electromagnetic waves]] in multiconductor systems. In 1988, he was a visiting professor at the [[Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)|Catholic University of Leuven]] for a year and became internationally known as an expert in electrical engineering.<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Keßelring |first=Agilolf |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VtOxEAAAQBAJ&dq=rusmir+mahmut%C4%87ehaji%C4%87&pg=PA90 |title=Die Bundeswehr auf dem Balkan: Zwischen Krieg und Friedenseinsatz |date=2023-03-06 |publisher=Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht |isbn=978-3-647-35222-0 |language=de}}</ref> 

From 1985 to 1991, he served as Professor and Dean of Electrical Engineering at the [[University of Osijek]] in Croatia.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Berman |first=Russell A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OjNBWahMyN8C&dq=rusmir+mahmutcehajic&pg=PA192 |title=Freedom or Terror: Europe Faces Jihad |date=2013-09-01 |publisher=Hoover Press |isbn=978-0-8179-1116-4 |language=en}}</ref>

He served as the Deputy Prime Minister of the [[Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina]] in 1992 and Energy Minister from 1992 to 1994, during the [[Bosnian War|Bosnian war]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Rusmir Mahmutćehajić |url=http://www.worldwisdom.com/public/authors/Rusmir-Mahmutcehajic.aspx |access-date=2023-04-22 |website=www.worldwisdom.com}}</ref> He was a close associate of [[Alija Izetbegović]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last1=Chitnis |first1=Rajendra A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m4_UDwAAQBAJ&dq=Rusmir+Mahmut%C4%87ehaji%C4%87+muslim&pg=PA33 |title=Translating the Literatures of Small European Nations |last2=Stougaard-Nielsen |first2=Jakob |last3=Atkin |first3=Rhian |last4=Milutinović |first4=Zoran |date=2019-12-31 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-1-78962-052-8 |language=en}}</ref> He later parted with Izetbegović and the [[Party of Democratic Action|SDA]] over the [[Dayton Agreement]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The historical construction of a Muslim threat underpinning the betrayal of Bosnia |url=https://crescent.icit-digital.org/articles/the-historical-construction-of-a-muslim-threat-underpinning-the-betrayal-of-bosnia |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=Crescent International}}</ref>

Mahmutćehajić served as a professor of electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and Islamic theology at the University of Sarajevo since 1995.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vZO0AAAAQBAJ&dq=Rusmir+Mahmut%C4%87ehaji%C4%87+deputy+prime+minister&pg=PR11|title=The War in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina 1991–1995|last1=Magas|first1=Branka|last2=Zanic|first2=Ivo|date=5 September 2013|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-34092-5|language=en}}</ref> He lived in [[Sarajevo]], where he worked as the president of International Forum Bosnia.<ref name="rusmirmahmutcehajic1" /> He is the author of more than 20 works in Bosnian, several of which have been translated to English, French, Italian, and Turkish.<ref name=":0" />

Mahmutćehajić died in Sarajevo on 6 April 2026, at the age of 77.<ref>{{cite web | title=Former Bosnian Deputy Prime Minister and Academic Rusmir Mahmutcehajic passes away in Sarajevo | website=n1 | date=6 April 2026 | url=https://n1info.ba/english/news/former-bosnian-deputy-prime-minister-and-academic-rusmir-mahmutcehajic-passes-away-in-sarajevo/ | access-date=7 April 2026}}</ref>

== Thought ==
Mahmutćehajić argued for a vision of Bosnia that is pluralistic and inclusive of racial, ethnic, and religious diversity.<ref name=":0" />

== Works ==
Mahmutćehajić was the author of more than 20 books and hundreds of essays and articles. His publications include:
* 1977 – ''Krhkost''
* 1996 – ''Suđeni Stolac''
* 2000 – ''Bosnia the Good: Tolerance and Tradition''
* 2000 – ''The Denial of Bosnia''
* 2003 – ''Sarajevo Essays: Politics, Ideology, and Tradition''
* 2005 – ''Learning from Bosnia: Approaching Tradition''
* 2006 – ''The Mosque: the Heart of Submission''
* 2007 – ''On Love: In the Muslim Tradition''
* 2011 – ''On the Other: A Muslim View''
* 2011 – ''Across the River: On the Poetry of [[Mak Dizdar]]''
* 2011 – ''Maintaining the Sacred Center: the Bosnian City of Stolac''
* 2015 – ''The Praised and the Virgin''
